article.headline: Alexandra Eala storms into WTA 250 Hong Kong Open quarterfinals after victory
article.summary: Filipino second seed Alexandra Eala defeated Tereza Valentova in two sets on Thursday to secure her spot in the tournament quarterfinals.
article.body:
Alexandra Eala secured a 6-4, 7-6 (7-0) victory against Czech opponent Tereza Valentova on the outdoor hardcourt at Victoria Park Tennis Stadium. This performance pushes the 19-year-old into the quarterfinals during the final WTA Tour event of 2026. Prior to this match, Eala navigated her first round by defeating Australian Emerson Jones in straight sets, 6-4, 6-3.

Advancing through the bracket is critical for Eala as the WTA Tour concludes its season. The Hong Kong Open acts as a final tune-up for participants, occurring simultaneously with the Chennai Open in India. Players are currently finalizing their form before the WTA Finals begin on November 8 at Indian Wells.

According to the Philippine News Agency, Eala will now face Croatian Antonia Ruzic, who reached this stage by defeating sixth seed Xinyu Wang. Other notable results from the event include fourth seed Maria Sakkari, who advanced by overcoming Maya Joint, and American Claire Liu, who bested British eighth seed Katie Boulter. Turkish competitor Zeynep Sonmez and Russian Alexandra Shubladze also booked their places in the next round after respective wins against Mika Stojsavljevic and Elena Pridankina.

The upcoming quarterfinal match against Ruzic will determine if Eala progresses to the final four. The tournament field remains competitive as top-ranked players vie for success in these last remaining matches before the season-ending competition in Indian Wells begins.

article.headline: Jobe Bellingham earns first senior England call-up under head coach Thomas Tuchel
article.summary: Thomas Tuchel has selected Jobe Bellingham for the senior England squad to face Croatia and Spain in the Nations League.
article.body: Borussia Dortmund midfielder Jobe Bellingham joins the senior setup after U21 head coach Lee Carsley spoke highly of his performance for weeks and months. His inclusion marks a significant elevation to the senior squad as England prepares for upcoming Nations League fixtures. This selection highlights the competitive nature of the current squad, as Tuchel opts to bring in fresh faces while leaving out established players such as Phil Foden, Kobbie Mainoo, and Cole Palmer. The decision to include Bellingham alongside Josh King follows a period where the England management team prioritized players who demonstrated consistency during previous camps. For fans and observers, the call-up signals an opportunity for Bellingham to translate his youth international experience into the senior level under Tuchel's leadership. The head coach emphasized that spots in the squad are earned through performance and presence in camp, noting that the competition for places remains high. According to Sky Sports, the 25-man roster features several changes including the return of Ben White and Djed Spence, while the team continues to manage various injuries within the group. The squad is now finalizing its preparations ahead of the critical Nations League matches against Croatia and Spain. As the international break approaches, focus shifts to how the new additions will integrate into the starting rotation. Tuchel's approach suggests that the door remains open for all players who show the required form and fitness, with the current camp acting as the primary evaluation point for future selection cycles.

news.title: Japan's Nikkei Posts Worst Weekly Loss Since 2020
news.og_title: Japan's Nikkei Posts Worst Weekly Loss Since 2020
news.og_desc:
Tokyo, November 06, 2026, SPA -- Japan's benchmark Nikkei 225 index dropped 9.3% this week, marking its worst weekly performance since March 2020, weighed down by a sharp tech sell-off following Wall Street losses and concerns over US policy impacts on artificial intelligence.
    On Friday, the index fell 6% to close at 57,434.77 points in its steepest single-day decline since April 2025, with 222 of its 225 constituent stocks retreating.
    The broader TOPIX index also shed 5.9%, with all 33 sector sub-indices closing lower.
    -- SPA
12:00 Local Time 09:00 GMT
